campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: Campbell's City Council considered routine business including paying city bills, accepting donations for the police K9 program, and approving new labor agreements with the police officers' union and a carpenters' union. The Council also reviewed a bond oversight committee report, discussed voting representation for an upcoming statewide conference, and considered a pay increase for the City Clerk.
keyTopics: Approval of bills and claims totaling $3,599,705.93
Acceptance of $41,911.62 in Campbell Police Foundation donations for K9 veterinary care and equipment
New labor agreements (2026-2028) with the Campbell Peace Officers Association and North Coast States Carpenters Union
FY 2025 Annual Report from the Citizen's Bond Oversight Committee for Measure O
Designation of voting delegates for the League of California Cities Annual Conference and a merit pay increase for the City Clerk

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a routine set of items including meeting minutes, vendor payments, and a treasurer's report, alongside several contracts for city services like janitorial work, irrigation maintenance, and a GIS consultant. Larger items included a contested appeal of a Planning Commission decision on a 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road, a new five-year law enforcement agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, and budget amendments for the new fiscal year. The Council also reviewed parking restrictions, final map approvals for several lot splits, and equipment purchases to electrify city facilities.
keyTopics: Appeal of Planning Commission's denial of a 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road, including its Environmental Impact Report
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Contracts for Bellgrove Park playground replacement and irrigation maintenance for city landscaped areas
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive
Purchase of electric equipment to replace gas systems at Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several infrastructure and construction items, including roof replacement at the History Museum, EV chargers at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library patio project. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and reviewed two housing development proposals for new condominium projects on First Street and Sherwood/Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Vesting tentative maps for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street and 33 condominium units at Sherwood/Acacia Avenues
Contract award for History Museum roof replacement (not-to-exceed $147,500) and Maintenance Yard EV Chargers project (not-to-exceed $363,220)
Acceptance of the Woodland Library Patio Expansion project completion
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up routine business, including approval of prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and payroll records, along with a professional services agreement and an amendment to an existing contract. The Council also considered an omnibus ordinance to make minor updates to the Town Code, appointed a voting delegate for a League of California Cities event, and addressed a request related to continuing or hearing a public hearing appeal.
keyTopics: Professional services agreement authorization for the Town Manager
Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Voting delegate and alternate appointment for the League of California Cities Annual meeting
Omnibus ordinance amending the Town Code with minor updates
Second amendment to an existing agreement and a request to continue or hear a public hearing appeal

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural Rules and Open Government Committee meeting focused on organizing upcoming City Council agendas rather than debating policy. The Committee reviewed the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 Council meeting and considered a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment, while the September 8 meeting was cancelled.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 Council meeting agenda, including possible new items and time-certain scheduling
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review
Public record covering August 13–20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting planning with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met in a closed session to discuss personnel matters, including performance evaluations of two Council appointees—the City Clerk and City Manager—and labor negotiations concerning those unrepresented positions. The public had an opportunity to speak on non-agenda items before the closed session began.
keyTopics: Public comment period for items not on the agenda
Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations discussion involving Vice Mayor Clark as the designated representative for the City Clerk and City Manager positions

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, that began with a closed session followed by a public presentation. The presentation portion covered an update on the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session held prior to the public meeting
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event, a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, and a presentation from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also considered approving minutes from its June 10, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation from youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, with in-person attendance at City Hall and remote participation options via Zoom or phone. One councilmember, Chahal, participated remotely from India. The agenda excerpt provided does not include details on specific policy items or votes considered by the Council.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India
Meeting conducted in hybrid format with in-person and Zoom/phone options for public participation

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered an ordinance amending part of the city's municipal code and received an educational presentation on municipal bonds basics. The meeting also included routine items such as the council calendar, meeting minutes, and lists of upcoming and requested agenda items.
keyTopics: Ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation on Municipal Bonds 101
City Council calendar of upcoming meetings
Preview list of anticipated items for the next regular meeting
List of agenda items requested by councilmembers

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission considered final approval of a public art plan for the private development at 3150 El Camino Real, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and developer. The commission also considered funding for temporary interactive media art installations and the acceptance of donated artworks for the city's collection.
keyTopics: Final review and approval of public art plan for 3150 El Camino Real development, with presentation by art consultant Danielle Wohl, artist Giles Miller, and Acclaim Companies
Allocation of up to $70,000 from the Art in Public Places CIP fund for temporary Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
Approval of June 18, 2026 Public Art Commission meeting minutes
